Subject: Estimating committed capacity — Meridian demand profile attached

Hi Rishi / team,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As we talked through our roadmap, we want a proposal that balances a predictable baseline for inference with the ability to absorb periodic spikes from our ingestion pipeline. I've attached a short demand profile (hourly RPS and peak window assumptions) so you can map options to our traffic.

High level asks from our side:
- A minimum guaranteed capacity we can rely on for SLAs (model latency SLOs)
- A mechanism to handle 2–4x short spikes during launches / marketing pushes without manual escalation
- Clear decommit/scale-down triggers — we have limited budget for long-term locked commitments, so we prefer staged guarantees with fallbacks

Can you send 2–3 discrete reservation structures (cluster sizes, min GPUs, and ramp schedule) that we can evaluate with Finance? Ideally include rough monthly unit cost deltas for each.

Attachments: Meridian_Demand_Profile.csv (hourly forecast)

—Sofia
Head of Platform Engineering
Meridian Labs

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Estimating committed capacity — Meridian demand profile attached

Hi Sofia — thanks for the profile, that helped a lot. Putting three differentiated structures below so Meridian can pick against cost vs operational predictability. Attached is a one-page option summary (RI_OptionSummary_v1.pdf) and a draft word doc for the anchored-floor option.

Summary of three reservation structures (illustrative):

1) Anchored Floor (predictable, lower latency variance)
- Cluster size: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (single pool)
- Minimum guaranteed: 12 GPUs active (75% floor)
- Warm capacity: 4 GPUs available as warm spare for fast scaling (pre-warmed KV caches)
- Ramp schedule: 12 guaranteed from contract start; scale to full 16 across the first 60 days as traffic validates
- Decommit policy: step-down allowed after quarter boundary with 30 days notice if 30-day rolling utilization < 40%
- Typical use case: steady baseline traffic with occasional promotional spikes you want tight latency on

2) Elastic Burst Lane (cost-efficient burst capacity)
- Cluster size: 24 GPUs (logical lanes: 12 guaranteed, 12 burstable)
- Minimum guaranteed: 8 GPUs (conservative floor to keep unit cost lower)
- Burst model: additional lanes available at a pre-negotiated burst rate; burst capacity is best-effort but prioritized over on-demand
- Ramp schedule: 8 guaranteed day 1; +4 GPUs onboarding after week 2; burst lanes available immediately
- Decommit policy: guaranteed floor can reduce by up to 25% at quarter boundary with 60 days notice; burst lanes charged only when used
- Typical use case: unpredictable peaks where cost efficiency during lulls is a priority

3) Phased Warmstart (fast activation, shorter commit)
- Cluster size: 12 GPUs across two regions (6/6) for regional failover
- Minimum guaranteed: 6 GPUs (one regional pool)
- Warmstart buffer: 3 GPUs kept pre-warmed in each region during month 1, then adaptive based on weekly traffic signals
- Ramp schedule: 6 guaranteed day 1; +3 GPUs per 30-day period based on milestone triggers (volume thresholds)
- Decommit policy: 30-day rolling util trigger plus auto-fallback to hosted with predefined latency bands if commit reduced
- Typical use case: teams wanting a shorter-term commitment window and multiregional resilience

Estimated delta (very rough): Anchored Floor ~ +15–22% vs pure on-demand; Elastic Burst ~ +6–12% base with burst usage billed separately; Phased Warmstart ~ +10–18% depending on geo split and pre-warm settings. We'll surface a formal TCO once you confirm target floor and ramp tempo.

Questions for Meridian to choose variant:
- Which is more important: predictable latency (Anchored) or lower committed spend (Elastic)?
- Do you need fast regional failover or is single-region okay initially?
- Any constraints from Procurement on minimum contract term or decommit notice windows?

If this looks good I can convert to a short proposal with exact GPU SKU pricing and a DocuSign-ready signature page.

Attachments: RI_OptionSummary_v1.pdf, Meridian_Proposal_AnchoredFloor.docx

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Email: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Rishi — thanks for the options, very helpful. A couple of clarifying items before we loop in Finance: 

1) For Anchored Floor, what is the expected cold-start penalty if we exceed 16 GPUs? Is there a predictable fallback to hosted on-demand and what latency delta should we expect for overflow tokens?
2) For Elastic Burst, can you quantify the burst-rate premium (per-GPU / per-token) we should model for Finance?
3) For Phased Warmstart, please confirm the activation SLA for adding the +3 GPUs (is it 48 hours or 7 days?).

Our preference today is a conservative Anchored Floor for the first two quarters (latency is mission-critical), but Meridian also wants a decommit trigger that doesn't lock us beyond 6 months if traffic flattens. Can you give a concrete decommit example (dates/times/conditions) for the Anchored option?

Also, FYI — our Procurement team needs a simple checklist of what data Redwoods will provide for SOC2/compliance evidence during onboarding (logs, audit trails, HIPAA PII handling).

—Jamie
VP Engineering, Meridian Labs

Jamie / Sofia — good questions. Below are concrete numbers and an example decommit scenario for the Anchored Floor option, plus next steps and a link to a DocuSign starter if you want to lock a pilot.

Anchored Floor — specifics and example triggers
- SKU assumptions: A100-equivalent pricing used for baseline. Detailed SKU pricing will be in the formal quote.
- Cold-start overflow behavior: when cluster >16 required, requests overflow to the Redwood hosted on-demand pool. We maintain a routing priority so overflow traffic will see an incremental median latency increase of ~55–120ms depending on sequence lengths (we can provide per-model test vectors).
- Burst capacity shortfall: if >16 sustained for 20 continuous minutes, we recommend auto-burst to hosted at agreed burst rate to prevent queueing; this is an optional protection you can enable.

Concrete decommit example (how it would work):
- Contract starts: 2027-01-01, guaranteed floor = 12 GPUs.
- Utilization window observed: 2027-03-01 to 2027-03-31 (30-day rolling) average sustained utilization across the cluster = 33%.
- Decommit trigger: because <40% for 30-day rolling, Meridian may request a step-down at the quarter boundary (2027-04-01) to reduce guaranteed floor by up to 2 GPUs with 30 calendar days notice from Redwood; final change effective 2027-05-01.
- Grace credits: for one step-down per 12-month period, Redwood will apply a one-time service credit equal to 10% of that quarter's committed spend to cover reconfiguration and warmstart costs.

Burst pricing guidance (high-level):
- Burstable GPU lane premium: +0.28–0.45 USD per GPU-hour over base committed unit price (model dependent).
- Overflow to hosted on-demand: per-token billing at host pool rates; we will model your demand profile into a blended bill so Finance gets an expected monthly spend range.

Procurement / SOC2 checklist (short):
- Access logs and audit trails: exported at daily cadence (CSV + linkable retention policy)
- Key management: KMS integration options documented; HSM available on Private deployments
- Data residency: region locking options and VPC peering details
- Shared eval artifacts: test vectors and latency trace artifacts for baseline SLAs

Next steps:
1) If you want the Anchored Floor pilot: confirm floor (we suggested 12 GPUs), target start date (we recommend 2027-01-01), and whether you want auto-burst protection enabled.
2) We'll produce a DocuSign-ready pilot agreement and a formal TCO schedule. Draft DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/drive/sign?envelopeId=ABC123-MERIDIAN
3) Priyom / Laura from my team will schedule a 30-minute pricing walkthrough with your Finance and Procurement.

Let us know by EOD next Tuesday and we'll start the paperwork.

—Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
